title: Start of the interview and framing question on New Orleans influence
summary: Steiner identifies the interview (Chace, November 18, 1961) and asks what New Orleans influence remains on white Chicago players.

story.theme_name: Starting the tape: names, dates and places
story.community_name: Interview openings: names, dates and tape setup

blocks.x: I think of anybody who tried to copy Rapolo, can you?
Oh, I... He had a beautiful, clean style and everything, but... He seemed to be almost isolated.
This is an interview with Frank Chase. My name is John Steiner. This is Saturday, maybe the 18th of... Is it the 18th? About 18th of November 19th.

1961. Frank, being the principal member of a new school around Chicago, perpetuating the white school, which started in the 20s following the immigration of the New Orleans Jazz Men, who is, I felt, was a logical person to discourse on the remaining effects of New Orleans Jazz, in the action on the... the white style that he is playing at present. Do you think there's anybody from New Orleans at present Frank who influences the young fellas around Chicago? Do you recall any New Orleans people who are copied or who are listened to with special attention? Among white players playing today. By... By... By...
